A 2014 study from the Harvard School of Public Health (Oh et al., Journal of Nutrition) found that women who consumed instant noodles two or more times per week had a 68% higher risk of metabolic syndrome — a cluster of conditions including hypertension, insulin resistance, and abdominal obesity — independent of overall dietary quality. Cup Noodles (original flavor) contains 1,190 mg sodium per serving (52% of the daily recommended value), TBHQ (a preservative rated “Avoid” by CSPI’s Chemical Cuisine), MSG, sodium phosphates, and multiple artificial flavor compounds.

firms.name: Smithfield Foods (WH Group)
firms.summary: The world's largest pork processor and hog producer, headquartered in Smithfield, Virginia. Acquired by Chinese conglomerate WH Group (formerly Shuanghui International, HKEX: 288) in September 2013 for $7.1 billion — the largest Chinese acquisition of a US company at the time. Smithfield's processed pork portfolio — Eckrich smoked sausages, Armour Star canned meats, Farmland bacon, Gwaltney, John Morrell, and Nathan's Famous hot dogs — relies on sodium nitrite as a preservative and color fixative. CSPI's Chemical Cuisine rates sodium nitrite as 'Avoid' because it reacts with amines in stomach acid to form N-nitrosamines, potent carcinogens. In 2015, IARC classified consumption of processed meats — all of which require sodium nitrite for their characteristic cured color and flavor — as Group 1 carcinogenic to humans, the same tier as tobacco smoke. Smithfield generates over $15 billion in annual revenue and is one of the largest single distributors of sodium nitrite-preserved meats to American consumers. Smithfield ranked #1 nationally among 1,671 facilities in the food sector for total toxic releases in EPA's 2022 Toxics Release Inventory, with 4.9 million pounds released. In 2024, following installation of a $45 million wastewater treatment facility, the company still released 1.1 million pounds of nitrates and 51,400 pounds of ammonia into the Big Sioux River watershed. Nitrate and ammonia pollution from industrial meat processing contributes to algal blooms, dead zones, and contamination of drinking water sources. A Mercy For Animals undercover investigator who spent a month working at a Smithfield hog facility documented mother pigs confined for life in gestation crates too small to turn around in, many with untreated pressure sores and open wounds, and piglets taken from their mothers as young as 10 days old to have their tails docked and testicles removed without painkillers.

firms.name: Tesla, Inc.
firms.summary: Electric vehicle and clean energy company founded in 2003, controlled by CEO Elon Musk. DOJ documents released in January 2026 show Musk exchanged at least 16 emails with Jeffrey Epstein between 2012 and 2014, including discussions about visiting Epstein's private island ('heli to island'), a February 2013 SpaceX tour that Epstein attended with three assistants, and social topics. Despite Musk's 2019 claim that he refused to visit and knew Epstein was 'a creep,' the emails document multiple coordination attempts for Caribbean meetups. Musk has not been accused of wrongdoing related to Epstein. April 2024: Tesla laid off >10% of its global workforce — ~14,000 employees — amid its first YoY sales decline since the pandemic (Reuters / CNN Business). In February 2023 Tesla fired 30+ Buffalo Gigafactory workers one day after they announced a union drive; an April 2024 NLRB complaint alleged Tesla unlawfully implemented an IT policy to discourage organizing (CNBC). In Diaz v. Tesla, a Black Fremont contractor testified he was called the N-word 60+ times; the jury awarded $137M in 2021, later settled March 2024 (NPR). December 2023: NHTSA forced Tesla to recall ~2 million vehicles — nearly its entire US fleet — over an Autopilot driver-monitoring defect after a 2-year probe tied to ~1,000 crashes, some fatal (Washington Post). On the positive side, Greenly (independent) estimates Tesla's 2023 fleet displaced 10.2–14.4M metric tons CO2e — large, though 28–49% below Tesla's self-reported 20M-ton figure (CarbonCredits.com). Beyond the Epstein correspondence: Musk spent $250M+ backing Trump in the 2024 cycle ($238M to America PAC, $20.5M to the misleadingly-branded RBG PAC — the cycle's largest single donor, NBC News). As head of DOGE (Jan–Nov 2025) he engineered the largest peacetime federal workforce reduction on record — ~270,000 fewer workers — while a $2T savings claim was revised down to $150B and a former staffer's deposition admitted DOGE did not lower the deficit (Fortune).

The Paradise Papers (2017, ICIJ) revealed Apple restructured three Irish subsidiaries—Apple Sales International, Apple Operations International, and Apple Operations Europe—relocating the first two to Jersey after US Senate scrutiny exposed its previous 'Double Irish' tax arrangement. Apple Sales International alone generated over $120 billion in profits over five years (nearly 60% of Apple's worldwide earnings) while paying minimal tax. By 2017, Apple had accumulated $252 billion in offshore earnings through these structures. Appleby, the Bermuda law firm at the center of the Paradise Papers leak, facilitated the restructuring. The arrangement represents systemic elite impunity: the world's most profitable company used bespoke legal engineering to avoid public tax obligations that apply to ordinary businesses.
firms.blurb: Designs and sells iPhones, Macs, iPads, and runs the App Store and Apple services ecosystem.

firms.name: Nike, Inc.
firms.summary: Nike, Inc. is the world's largest athletic footwear and apparel company, headquartered in Beaverton, Oregon. The Paradise Papers (2017, ICIJ) revealed that Nike transferred approximately $1 billion annually to a Bermuda subsidiary tax-free, disguised as 'intra-group royalty fees' for the Swoosh trademark and other intellectual property. Nike's IP rights could be traced to a five-story office block in Bermuda occupied by Appleby and Estera—the law firm at the center of the Paradise Papers leak. Dutch tax authorities granted Nike a private 'tax ruling' that EU Competition Chief Margrethe Vestager found 'ignored economic reality,' determining that Nike paid too little tax in the Netherlands for 14 consecutive years and potentially owed over $1 billion in back taxes. Vestager found it inappropriate to classify the Bermuda unit as 'entrepreneurial' while Nike's Dutch workforce exceeded 9,000 employees (13% of its global staff).
firms.blurb: Designs and sells athletic footwear, apparel, and sports equipment under the Nike and Jordan brands.

firms.name: Uber Technologies, Inc.
firms.summary: Uber Technologies, Inc. operates the world's largest ride-hailing and food delivery platform. The Paradise Papers (2017, ICIJ) revealed that Uber routed profits through Bermuda to avoid taxes, with the core taxi-hailing app intellectual property traced to a Bermuda office block occupied by Appleby and Estera. A Dutch subsidiary later purchased the IP from the Bermuda shell company using a $16 billion intra-company loan from Uber's Singapore unit. The Uber Files (2022, ICIJ)—a separate leak of 124,000 internal documents—revealed that Uber's leadership, including then-CEO Travis Kalanick, authorized the use of a 'kill switch' to cut off data access during law enforcement raids in multiple countries, and that Uber conducted secret lobbying campaigns with heads of state, including private messages to then-French Economy Minister Emmanuel Macron, to undermine local taxi regulations.

firms.name: Anil Dhirubhai Ambani Group (ADAG)
firms.summary: Indian conglomerate controlled by billionaire Anil Ambani, named in the ICIJ Pandora Papers (October 2021) for offshore shell companies. In February 2020, Ambani declared bankruptcy before a UK court, claiming net worth of zero while owing $716 million to Chinese state banks—the Pandora Papers later documented his offshore financial holdings. A Mumbai court held him in criminal contempt in 2019 for failing to repay Reliance Communications debts to Ericsson; his brother Mukesh bailed him out to prevent imprisonment. Group subsidiaries Reliance Communications and Reliance Capital both collapsed into insolvency.
firms.blurb: Indian conglomerate with interests in power generation, infrastructure, and financial services.

The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP), through the ICIJ Pandora Papers investigation, documented how Chemezov's relatives were enriched through offshore shell companies. 2021 revenue: $28 billion.

firms.name: SOCAR (State Oil Company of Azerbaijan Republic)
firms.summary: Azerbaijan's national oil and gas company, the primary revenue instrument of President Ilham Aliyev's authoritarian government. The Aliyev family was named in the ICIJ Pandora Papers (2021): documents revealed offshore shell companies used to acquire over £66 million in UK real estate, including property gifted to an 11-year-old son. SOCAR ranked dead last (44th of 44) in Transparency International's 2011 anti-corruption survey of oil companies. Two SOCAR subsidiaries embezzled $1.7 billion from a BP contract. SOCAR made illegal payments of €28,000 to Germany's CDU and secretly funded US Congressional trips (~$750,000 through nonprofits). Associates were convicted in the US in 2009 for paying $11 million in bribes connected to SOCAR's privatization. SOCAR's Maltese chief was arrested as a main suspect in the 2017 murder of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia.

firms.summary: Beverly Hills PE firm with ~$90 billion AUM that finances acquisitions with heavy leverage. Acquired WellPet (now Wellness Pet Company) in November 2020, financing the deal with $985 million in term loans ($750M first-lien, $235M second-lien) on a ~$1.7 billion enterprise value. By 2025 the pet food company's capital structure collapsed: S&P downgraded its credit citing 'very high leverage, deeply distressed debt trading levels, and negative free operating cash flow,' and the company completed a distressed debt exchange in June 2025 in which first-lien lenders took only 80 cents on the dollar. Bloomberg reported in July 2024 that Clearlake's distressed debt pile across its portfolio exceeded $10 billion — the consequence of routine LBO debt-loading.

firms.name: Sinclair Broadcast Group
firms.summary: Sinclair Broadcast Group, based in Hunt Valley, Maryland, is the second-largest television station operator in the United States with approximately 185 stations reaching roughly 40% of US television households. Controlled by David D. Smith and his brothers through a dual-class stock structure, Sinclair received the largest civil penalty in FCC history at the time (May 2020) — a $48 million fine — after regulators found the company used shell companies (Cunningham Broadcasting) to circumvent FCC media ownership limits and made material misrepresentations during its attempt to acquire Tribune Media for $3.9 billion. The FCC order also found that 64 Sinclair stations aired paid sponsored content as local news more than 1,400 times without disclosure. From 2017 to December 2019, Sinclair required all its local stations to air 'must-run' political commentary segments hosted by Boris Epshteyn, a former Trump campaign and White House aide, centralizing partisan propaganda across nominally independent local news outlets.

firms.name: iHeartMedia
firms.summary: iHeartMedia (formerly Clear Channel Communications) is the largest commercial radio broadcaster in the United States, operating over 860 stations. In 2008, Bain Capital and Thomas H. Lee Partners took Clear Channel private in a leveraged buyout valued at approximately $17.9 billion, loading the company with $20+ billion in total debt. The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in March 2018 carrying roughly $20.6 billion in debt — one of the largest media bankruptcies in US history. Despite the bankruptcy, the PE sponsors broke even by purchasing company debt at deep discounts and extracting management fees over the decade-long holding period, while creditors absorbed the losses. The company reorganized and re-emerged publicly in 2019. iHeartMedia's ownership of over 860 radio stations under consolidated programmatic syndication has hollowed out local radio journalism while maintaining the appearance of local reach.

firms.name: Nexstar Media Group
firms.summary: Nexstar Media Group, based in Irving, Texas, is the largest local television broadcaster in the United States with approximately 200 stations across 116 markets, reaching about 68% of US television households. CEO Perry Sook earned over $40 million in 2022 — the highest compensation of any executive in the Dallas–Fort Worth area — and $35.9 million in 2024, while the company simultaneously reduced local newsroom staffing through automation and layoffs. In 2023, workers at Nexstar's Rochester, NY station WROC voted to unionize, but Nexstar refused to recognize the union and contested the vote in court, according to the NewsGuild-CWA. Nexstar acquired WGN America as part of its $4.1 billion Tribune Media purchase and rebranded it as NewsNation in 2021. Nexstar has lobbied aggressively to weaken FCC media ownership rules to enable further consolidation.

firms.name: McDonald's Corporation
firms.summary: World's largest fast food company by revenue, headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, operating approximately 40,000 restaurants in over 100 countries with annual revenues exceeding $23 billion. McDonald's core menu items are NOVA Group 4 ultra-processed foods per the Monteiro et al. classification: French fries contain sodium acid pyrophosphate (added to prevent post-fry discoloration), dimethylpolysiloxane (a silicone antifoam agent in the frying oil), and 'natural beef flavoring' derived from hydrolyzed wheat and hydrolyzed milk — industrial ingredients absent from home-cooked potatoes. Chicken McNuggets contain sodium phosphates, modified food starch, and autolyzed yeast extract, which are markers of industrial food formulation. These additives standardize color, texture, and palatability at global scale rather than serving safety or nutritional functions, placing the items firmly in NOVA Group 4 per the Public Health Nutrition classification system (Monteiro et al. 2019). Flagged under health_general.

firms.name: Crow Holdings
firms.summary: Crow Holdings is the Dallas-based private real estate investment empire of billionaire Harlan Crow. Over more than two decades, Crow secretly provided Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas with undisclosed luxury gifts — including private jet travel, superyacht vacations, stays at Crow's private Adirondacks resort Camp Topridge, and a 2014 real estate transaction involving property belonging to Thomas's family — worth hundreds of thousands of dollars, without Thomas disclosing the gifts as required by post-Watergate federal ethics law. ProPublica's 2023 investigation documented that Thomas failed to report the gifts, likely violating the Ethics in Government Act. Senate Finance Committee requests for a full accounting were rebuffed by Crow. No criminal charges were filed against either Thomas or Crow, exemplifying how concentrated wealth buys unchecked access to the highest court in the country.

firms.name: FTX Trading Ltd
firms.summary: FTX Trading Ltd was the Bahamas-based parent of the FTX cryptocurrency exchange, founded by Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF) in 2019. FTX grew to a peak valuation of 2 billion before collapsing in November 2022 when it was revealed Bankman-Fried had misappropriated approximately  billion in customer funds to cover losses at affiliated hedge fund Alameda Research. FTX insiders made 30 million in political donations — including 0 million from SBF to Democratic campaigns and hidden dark-money donations to Republicans — explicitly to purchase regulatory access and impunity; SBF met privately with SEC Chair Gary Gensler in March 2022 while lobbying for favorable legislation. Bankman-Fried cultivated an "effective altruist" public image to deflect scrutiny. He was convicted on all seven federal fraud and conspiracy counts in November 2023 and sentenced to 25 years in federal prison in March 2024, with over 1 billion in forfeiture ordered (U.S. v. Bankman-Fried, SDNY).

firms.name: Wirecard AG
firms.summary: Wirecard AG was a Munich-based payment processing company that was once Germany's most valuable fintech, reaching a market cap exceeding €24 billion on the DAX index. In June 2020 the company admitted that €1.9 billion in reported Asian escrow accounts — roughly a quarter of its balance sheet — did not exist, representing one of the largest accounting frauds in post-war German history. Germany's financial regulator BaFin actively shielded the company from scrutiny for years: it received whistleblower tips in January 2019 and waited more than a year to act, while filing criminal complaints against Financial Times journalists and short-sellers who raised alarms. Chief Operating Officer Jan Marsalek fled Germany by private jet to Belarus before arrest warrants were issued; Russian FSB agents escorted him to Moscow, where he lives today under the false identity "Alexander Nelidov," per joint investigations by Der Spiegel, PBS Frontline, ZDF, and The Insider (2025). 6,000 employees lost their jobs in the collapse.

firms.name: Kao Corporation
firms.summary: Kao Corporation is a Japanese consumer goods company headquartered in Tokyo, founded in 1887, with global annual sales exceeding ¥1.5 trillion (~$10B USD). Kao markets personal care, hair care, and household products under brands including Bioré, John Frieda, and Jergens. Kao states it 'complies with regulations' around animal testing — meaning the company conducts or commissions animal testing when required by law, including to meet pre-market testing requirements for imported cosmetics sold in mainland China. Kao is not certified cruelty-free by Leaping Bunny (Cruelty Free International) or PETA, and is documented by multiple cruelty-free watchdog organizations as not cruelty-free due to its China market presence and testing policy.

firms.name: NSO Group
firms.summary: NSO Group Technologies is an Israeli cybersurveillance firm and developer of the Pegasus spyware, capable of silently exfiltrating all data from a target smartphone without user interaction. The company was purchased by U.S. private equity firm Francisco Partners for $130 million in 2014, then reacquired by its co-founders with backing from London private equity fund Novalpina Capital at approximately a $1 billion valuation in 2019. NSO sold Pegasus to at least a dozen authoritarian governments including Saudi Arabia—whose agents used it to surveil associates of journalist Jamal Khashoggi before his 2018 murder—as well as the UAE, Mexico, Bahrain, and Morocco, targeting journalists, lawyers, and opposition politicians. WhatsApp (Meta) sued NSO in October 2019 for deploying Pegasus to hack approximately 1,400 users, and a jury awarded Meta $168 million in damages in May 2025. The U.S. Department of Commerce added NSO to its Entity List in November 2021, citing actions contrary to U.S. national security interests. Despite widespread documented harms enabling authoritarian surveillance of dissidents and journalists, NSO's principals faced no criminal prosecution in Israel.

firms.name: Black Cube
firms.summary: Black Cube is an Israeli private intelligence firm founded in 2010 by former Israeli military intelligence officers Avi Yanus and Dan Zorella, with an advisory board that has included former Mossad directors Meir Dagan and Efraim Halevy. The firm operates as a for-hire corporate espionage service, deploying operatives under false identities to surveil, record, and discredit targets on behalf of wealthy clients. The firm gained international notoriety in November 2017 when Ronan Farrow's New Yorker investigation revealed Harvey Weinstein paid Black Cube to deploy an 'army of spies'—including agents posing as women's-rights advocates—to record and discredit his sexual-assault accusers and the journalists covering them, including Rose McGowan. Canadian litigation records (Globe and Mail, June 2021) disclosed 'Project Maple Tree': Toronto hedge fund Catalyst Capital paid approximately $11 million CAD for Black Cube to run an operation designed to entrap and discredit Ontario Justice Frank Newbould after he ruled against Catalyst in a business dispute. The firm has also documented political-opposition surveillance operations for former Congo President Joseph Kabila.

firms.name: Psy-Group
firms.summary: Psy-Group was an Israeli private intelligence and influence-operations firm founded on December 22, 2014, employing primarily former Israeli military intelligence officers. The firm specialized in social media manipulation, fake-persona creation, honey traps, and bespoke political disinformation campaigns for government and corporate clients. On August 3, 2016, Psy-Group owner Joel Zamel met Donald Trump Jr., UAE intermediary George Nader, and Blackwater founder Erik Prince at Trump Tower to pitch a social media manipulation campaign against Hillary Clinton. After Trump won the election, Nader paid Zamel up to $2 million. Mueller's investigators scrutinized Psy-Group's ties to the Trump campaign and to Saudi and UAE-aligned influence operations. Psy-Group also signed a partnership agreement with Cambridge Analytica in December 2016 and ran 'Project Butterfly,' an anti-BDS disinformation campaign. The firm operated through layered offshore accounts including Cyprus-based IOCO and Swiss-managed entities to obscure ownership. Psy-Group shut down in 2018 after its operations were exposed, with no criminal accountability for its principals.

Its subsidiary Cambridge Analytica harvested personal data from approximately 87 million Facebook users without consent — obtained via Aleksandr Kogan's personality quiz app — and used that data to build voter profiles for micro-targeted political advertising, including for the 2016 US presidential election and the Brexit campaign. In March 2018, Channel 4 filmed SCL executives Alexander Nix and Mark Turnbull boasting about using bribery, honey traps, and sex workers to entrap politicians and swing elections. UK ICO convicted SCL Elections Ltd of breaching the Data Protection Act; the FTC reached a consent order with CEO Alexander Nix imposing 20-year restrictions on his business practices and requiring destruction of all improperly obtained data. In 2018, the Gates Foundation and other investors commissioned an audit after raising concerns about missing money; the audit revealed that Abraaj had commingled investor funds and misappropriated at least hundreds of millions of dollars to disguise liquidity shortfalls and for personal benefit, while inflating fund values by more than half a billion dollars to attract new investors. Abraaj was forced into liquidation in June 2018. In April 2019, the U.S. Department of Justice arrested Naqvi in the UK and charged him with wire fraud, securities fraud, and money laundering; the SEC filed parallel civil charges. Naqvi was not expelled from the Giving Pledge until December 2024 — six years after the fraud became public — illustrating how philanthropic status within elite networks confers sustained impunity.

firms.name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG
firms.summary: Raiffeisen Bank International AG (RBI) is an Austrian banking group and one of the largest commercial banks in Central and Eastern Europe, headquartered in Vienna. Following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022, RBI stood out among Western financial institutions by continuing to operate its large Russian subsidiary, ZAO Raiffeisenbank, and refusing to exit the market. An OCCRP and Paper Trail Media investigation found that RBI sent 189 cash shipments totaling $10 billion to Russia in early 2022, including 10 shipments that arrived on or after the date of the invasion. RBI's Russian subsidiary thereby became the dominant channel for Russian clients to move money after other major Western banks withdrew. As of January 2025, RBI's investment arm Raiffeisen Capital held approximately 31.7 billion rubles ($365 million) in sanctioned Russian entities, including Sberbank and the state energy giant Gazprom. In 2024, the US Treasury issued a direct warning to RBI over a planned €1.35 billion stake transfer linked to sanctioned oligarch Oleg Deripaska; RBI abandoned the deal only after the warning. Despite sustained pressure from OCCRP, BankTrack, and the B4Ukraine coalition, RBI continued to serve as the premier financial lifeline for Russia's sanctioned economy, operating with impunity inside the Western financial system.

In June 2025, Founders Fund led the largest investment in its history — a $1 billion stake in Anduril's $2.5 billion Series G at a $30.5 billion valuation. Thiel additionally co-founded Dialog in 2006 with data entrepreneur Auren Hoffman, an invitation-only off-the-record network that convenes sitting U.S. senators, Trump administration officials, NATO commanders, intelligence figures, and founders of the country's largest surveillance and data-broker companies. In June 2026, internal records from Dialog — names, mobile numbers, birthdates, and emergency contacts of 222 registrants — were exposed after a website security lapse, revealing a concentrated intersection of political and surveillance-industry power operating entirely outside public accountability. Founders Fund portfolio companies (Palantir, Anduril, SpaceX) formed a defense-tech consortium in late 2024 to compete with traditional defense contractors; in 2025, U.S. budget language for border surveillance towers was written to technical specifications only Anduril could fulfill, drawing criticism that Thiel's political access was steering government contracts to his own portfolio companies.

firms.name: KPMG International Limited
firms.summary: KPMG is one of the Big Four professional services firms, providing audit, tax, and advisory services across 143 countries. In June 2019, KPMG agreed to pay a $50 million civil penalty to the SEC — which called the conduct 'astonishing' — after former KPMG partners obtained confidential PCAOB inspection data to identify which audits would be reviewed, then altered prior audit work papers to reduce the likelihood of deficiency findings before those inspections. The scheme also involved systemic cheating on internal training exams: audit professionals manipulated a training server so they could achieve passing scores while answering fewer than 25% of questions correctly. In a parallel scandal, KPMG South Africa was embedded in the Gupta family's state-capture operation under President Zuma, providing auditing and tax advisory services to Gupta-linked Linkway Trading — the conduit for laundering approximately R30 million stolen from a South African government agricultural subsidy scheme to fund the Gupta family's 2013 wedding. KPMG South Africa repaid R23 million (~$1.5M USD) in SARS fees and donated R40 million (~$2.7M USD) in Gupta-related fees; no criminal charges were filed against the firm or its partners in either jurisdiction despite the documented misconduct.

firms.name: Equifax Inc.
firms.summary: Equifax Inc. is one of the three major U.S. consumer credit bureaus, collecting and selling financial data on approximately 800 million consumers worldwide without those individuals' meaningful consent. In September 2017, Equifax announced a data breach that exposed the personal information — Social Security numbers, birth dates, addresses, driver's license numbers, and credit card numbers — of approximately 147.9 million Americans, roughly 56% of all American adults. The breach resulted from Equifax's failure to patch a known Apache Struts vulnerability (CVE-2017-5638) for more than two months after its public disclosure; separately, a security scan tool that should have detected the intrusion had been non-functional for 19 months due to an expired TLS certificate. CEO Richard Smith 'retired' in September 2017 with a compensation package potentially worth up to $90 million. In July 2019, Equifax agreed to pay at least $575 million — and up to $700 million — in a settlement with the FTC, CFPB, and 50 states and territories, the largest-ever FTC data security settlement at the time. The FBI opened a criminal investigation into the breach, but no executive at Equifax has ever been criminally charged for the negligence, delayed disclosure, or security failures that enabled it — a textbook case of corporate executives escaping accountability for harms that affected more than half of all American adults.

A 2023 comprehensive review (Nowak et al., PMC10535526) documented nine energy drink–associated cardiac arrests, three of them fatal, and found 'a robust correlation between the caffeine levels in energy drinks and adverse health and safety consequences,' recommending restrictions on minors' access. The Coca-Cola Company holds approximately 20.9% of Monster's outstanding shares and serves as its global distribution partner.

firms.name: ESL Investments

Lampert used ESL to acquire Kmart out of its 2002 bankruptcy, then merged it with Sears in 2005 to form Sears Holdings, which he ran as chairman and eventually CEO. In 2015, Lampert spun off 235 of Sears Holdings' most profitable store properties into a separate REIT, Seritage Growth Properties, in a $2.7 billion sale-leaseback deal; ESL held a 43.5% stake in Seritage while Sears was left paying Seritage roughly $349 million in rent on stores it had previously owned outright. Sears Holdings' workforce fell from about 317,000 employees in 2005 to about 68,000 by the time it filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October 2018 (Fortune). Lampert's ESL then bought the surviving Sears and Kmart stores out of bankruptcy through a new entity, Transformco, in 2019, keeping Lampert in control of what remained.

brands.why: Pilgrim's Pride Ultimate Chicken Nuggets, produced by JBS USA's majority-owned Pilgrim's Pride (64% stake since 2010), are classified as NOVA Group 4 ultra-processed foods. The nuggets are marinated, mechanically formed, tempura-battered, breaded, and par-fried before freezing — a multi-stage industrial process typical of ultra-processed meat products. Ingredients include chicken breast with rib meat, water, modified cornstarch, sodium phosphates, dextrose, salt, and flavoring. Sodium phosphates are processing aids used to retain moisture and enhance texture; high-phosphate diets have been linked to cardiovascular disease risk in a 2012 JAMA Internal Medicine study. Each serving contains 400-500mg of sodium (20-25% of recommended daily intake), contributing to hypertension risk. Research published in BMJ in 2026 found that ultra-processed foods were associated with a 47% higher risk of heart attack or stroke. Pilgrim's Pride chicken products generate billions in annual revenue as the second-largest U.S. poultry brand.

brands.why: Pepsi-Cola is classified as NOVA Group 4 ultra-processed food. A standard 12 oz can contains 41g of added sugar — exceeding the American Heart Association's entire daily recommended limit of 25g for women and approaching the 36g daily limit for men. The caramel color (Class IV) used in Pepsi-Cola contains 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI), a compound the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) classifies as possibly carcinogenic to humans (Group 2B). A 2015 study published in PLOS ONE and indexed on PubMed (PMC4333292, Lim et al.) found that per 12-oz serving of tested Pepsi products, 4-MEI exposures exceeded the level associated with one excess cancer case per 10,000 exposed individuals — above California Proposition 65 thresholds. California lists 4-MEI under Proposition 65 as a chemical known to cause cancer. Regular consumption of sugar-sweetened beverages is associated with a 26% higher risk of type 2 diabetes per Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health meta-analyses.

brands.blurb: Powdered and liquid non-dairy coffee creamer sold in original and flavored varieties.
brands.why: Coffee-Mate is classified as NOVA Group 4 ultra-processed food. The Original powdered formula lists corn syrup solids as its primary ingredient, followed by vegetable oil (coconut and/or palm kernel), sodium caseinate (a milk derivative), mono- and diglycerides, dipotassium phosphate, sodium aluminosilicate, and artificial flavor — a fully formulated industrial product with no unprocessed-food counterpart. The EWG Food Scores database rates Coffee-Mate Original poorly, citing nutrition concerns from corn syrup solids and saturated fat from palm and coconut kernel oils, as well as ingredient-level concerns from artificial flavor and the presence of mono- and diglycerides, which can carry residual trans fatty acids. Mono- and diglycerides are exempt from trans-fat labeling requirements even after the FDA's 2018 ban on partially hydrogenated oils, meaning products like Coffee-Mate can contribute trans fat not declared on the nutrition facts panel. Coffee-Mate is the top-selling coffee creamer brand in the United States, with annual US retail sales estimated above $1 billion.

During the January 2021 GameStop short squeeze, its affiliated hedge fund Citadel LLC invested .75 billion in heavily shorted Melvin Capital on January 25; the following day, Robinhood—which routes orders to Citadel Securities via PFOF—halted purchases of GameStop and related meme stocks. House Financial Services Committee hearings documented the conflict of interest but resulted in no regulatory consequences. Owner Ken Griffin donated over 00 million to Republican candidates and causes between 2020 and 2024 while lobbying aggressively against SEC proposals to reform PFOF—rules that would have directly curtailed Citadel Securities' revenue model. The SEC's PFOF reform proposals were ultimately shelved under the subsequent administration.

Ingredient documentation on Open Food Facts and academic NOVA classification guides consistently place boxed mac and cheese in the ultra-processed category due to its combination of isolated dairy proteins, industrial emulsifiers, and synthetic colorants not found in a home kitchen.
